standard.title: Connect personal and character experiences
standard.description: discuss connections between personal experiences and character experiences in literary texts
standard.prior_knowledge: Students identify features of literary texts and give reasons for personal preferences (AC9E2LE02). They have not yet focused specifically on drawing connections between their own experiences and those of characters — using prior knowledge and personal experience as a reading resource.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students discuss connections between their own experiences and the experiences of characters in literary texts.

nodes.label: Drawing on prior knowledge to connect
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can draw on relevant prior knowledge and personal experience to make meaningful connections to characters' situations in texts.
nodes.minimum_width: Identify one connection between a character's experience in a text and a personal or known experience, and discuss what the connection helps them understand.
nodes.typical_width: Discuss relevant prior knowledge and past experiences to make meaningful connections to characters in texts — explaining how personal experience helps understand what a character might feel or do.
wider: Compare connections made by different students to the same character — discussing how different experiences lead to different connections and what this reveals about reading as a personal act
Explore a text where a character's experience is very different from one's own, and discuss how to make connections despite the unfamiliarity

response_modes.reason: Making a meaningful connection requires more than naming a similarity — students need the reasoning chain: this happened to the character → something similar happened to me → this helps me understand that the character felt/did X. The 'so what' of the connection needs explicit scaffolding.

success_criteria: Student names a specific connection between their experience and a character's situation (not just 'I've been sad too')
Student explains how the connection helps them understand something about the character

nodes.label: Preferences grounded in experience
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can select and discuss favourite texts, explaining their preferences in ways that connect to personal experience and feelings.
nodes.minimum_width: Select a favourite text and explain at least one reason for the preference that connects to a personal experience or feeling.
nodes.typical_width: Select and discuss favourite texts, explaining reasons for assigning greater or lesser value — connecting preferences to what the text made them feel or reminded them of from their own experience.
wider: Compare preferences for the same text across a group and discuss why people connect differently — examining what different personal experiences lead to different preferences
Revisit a text that wasn't initially a favourite after a new personal experience, and discuss whether the connection changed
success_criteria: Student states a preference for a text and gives a reason (not just 'I liked it')
Student connects the preference to a personal experience or feeling the text evoked
